context: Re-run TPC-H SF>=1 on all four modes on an otherwise idle machine, n>=5 per mode, and replace the table in the ADR Status block. If the local bimodality disappears, say so explicitly; if it does not, that is a real finding about the local path and deserves its own item.
description: The maturity ADR's Status block publishes Power@Size means and CVs for the four DuckLake deployment modes and explicitly says 'Re-measure on a quiet host before treating these CVs as authoritative'. Nothing tracks that. The numbers were taken on a laptop running several concurrent agent sessions, and the local mode's series is bimodal (~98k on the first run, ~77k on repeats) - a systematic first-run-versus-later split rather than random variance, i.e. host contention. They are sound enough to support the conclusion they were used for (remote-backed runs are NOT materially less reproducible than local, confirming ADR decision w12) and not sound enough to quote as reproducibility characteristics of the platform.

deferrals.reason: Load averages 3.9/4.8/5.2 with a concurrent session's pytest at 99% CPU and Codex at 82% during the follow-up sweep; the item's own rule says a contended-host measurement is worse than none. Left pending for a genuinely quiet window.

preserves.behavior: ADR decision w12 stays confirmed unless the new numbers actually contradict it

verifications.description: The ADR no longer carries the provisional-measurement caveat
verifications.expected: caveat removed once the table is re-measured
